tickets.title: US001 (Student)
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want to search for available courses by keyword, so that I can quickly find classes that match my interests.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Given a keyword, the system returns a list of courses containing that keyword in title or description.
- Search results must display course name, code, and schedule.
- If no courses match, the system shows “No results found.”

tickets.title: US002 (Student)
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want to drag and drop courses into my calendar, so that I can visualize my weekly schedule.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Dragging a course into the calendar displays its time slot.
- If a conflict exists, the system highlights the overlap in red.
- Removing a course from the calendar clears its time slot.

tickets.title: US003 (Student)
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want to filter courses by prerequisites, so that I only see classes I am eligible to enroll in.
Acceptance Criteria:
-Filter option hides courses where prerequisites are not met.
-Eligible courses remain visible.
-The filter can be toggled on or off.

tickets.title: US004 (Administrator/Staff)
tickets.description:
As an Administrator, I want to override a student’s course selection, so that I can enforce institutional requirements.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Admin can view a student’s current schedule.
- Admin can replace or remove a course.
- The system logs the override action with timestamp and admin ID.

tickets.title: US005 (Student)
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want to receive notifications when a course I added becomes full, so that I can adjust my schedule promptly.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The system sends a notification when enrollment reaches capacity.
- Notification includes course name and code.
- Student can choose to remove the course or stay on the waitlist.

analysis.ambiguity1: Requirement: “The system should allow advisors to override student choices.” Why vague: The requirement does not specify the scope of the override. Advisors might be able to change all of a student’s course selections or only certain ones. It is also unclear whether the system should record these overrides for accountability. Without clarification, developers cannot determine the exact scope of functionality to implement.
analysis.ambiguity2: Requirement: “Drag and drop classes into a calendar to see if they fit.”  Why vague: The requirement does not clearly define what “fit” means. It could mean checking only for schedule conflicts, but it might also include verifying prerequisites, course availability, or other academic constraints. Without clarification, developers cannot determine the exact scope of functionality to implement.
analysis.conflictSolution: There is a conflict between the Registrar and the Head of Advising. The Registrar requires that students cannot add full classes to their roadmap, while the Head of Advising wants students to plan courses years ahead even when availability is unknown. The resolution is to allow students to add future courses with a status label such as 'Availability unknown.' When live data is available, the system updates the status. If a course is full, the student cannot enroll in it, but it can remain in the roadmap for planning purposes.
analysis.nfr1: Security: Protect student data and ensure privacy by preventing access to other students’ schedules and logging advisor overrides.
analysis.nfr2: Performance/Scalability: Ensure real-time responsiveness when linking to the live database.
analysis.nfr3: Usability: Provide an intuitive, user-friendly interface with drag-and-drop functionality for planning classes. and support long-term planning across multiple years.
